node.title: Re: Perl is ignoring fractional part sometimes
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [jinnicky],

Although I'm no [mod://Tk] expert, I investigated the AM's [id://1167934|hint] about dual-valued variables, and there indeed seems to be something buggy going on. I boiled the code down to the following:

use warnings; use strict; use Tk; use Devel::Peek; my $scale = '22.5 '; # note the space in the output as well my $foo = 0 + $scale; # use in numeric context (set NV and IV) Dump($scale); my $mw = MainWindow->new; $mw->Entry(-textvariable=>\$scale)->pack; $mw->bind("",\&calc); calc(); MainLoop; sub calc { print "str: <$scale> / num: <".(0+$scale)."> \n"; }

Output:

SV = PVNV(0x1e3f350) at 0x1e59a40 REFCNT = 2 FLAGS = (NOK,POK,IsCOW,pIOK,pNOK,pPOK) IV = 22 NV = 22.5 PV = 0x1e6f870 "22.5 "\0 CUR = 5 LEN = 10 COW_REFCNT = 1 str: <22.5 > / num: <22>

It appears that binding $scale to the [mod://Tk::Entry] widget is causing the variable to become dual-valued with the wrong initial values (I guess the PV and IV values?). This only seems to be happening once on init though, when I input something everything seems to work fine. I don't know enough about the internals of [mod://Tk] to really suggest a solution (perhaps a bug report is in order), but some workaround(s). You apparently can initialize $scale with a numeric value to begin with, my $scale = 22.5; seems to work for me. Or, as you've already discovered, you can stringify $scale when reading it out.

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
